name: Boerhavia

curation_status.status: morphology-first provisional; fruit macro photos pending

look_here_first: Find a mature anthocarp first. Check for stalked glands versus glabrous surface, then the shape of its five ribs and grooves. Next compare fruit apex, perianth and stamens; do not rely on flower color or leaf width.
shared_genus_traits: Tiny clustered flowers with a single petaloid perianth whorl (no separate corolla).
One-seeded fruit enclosed by the persistent basal perianth (anthocarp), typically prominently five-ribbed.
Leaf and flower color variation makes mature fruit characters especially important.

species_comparison_matrix.erecta: Diffuse branching clusters, fruit apex truncate/low-conic

quick_comparison_steps: Collect mature fruits from several branches; use a hand lens and millimeter scale.
Separate densely glandular B. coccinea from glabrous B. erecta/B. linearifolia.
Among glabrous fruits, inspect rib shape, grooves, and fruit apex.
Photograph flower clusters, perianth, stamens and full plant as supporting evidence.
overlap_and_cautions: B. diffusa and the B. intermedia / B. triquetra var. intermedia complex need separate keyed comparison before firm IDs.
All three currently have UNRESOLVED project target-zone range; Texas state-level native is not the project PASS threshold.
Current one-photo set shows flower/habit but not definitive mature fruit macros.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched scale-bearing mature anthocarp macro for each species
B. coccinea vs B. diffusa stalked-glandular fruit surface
B. erecta vs intermedia cluster and pedicel insertion
B. linearifolia perianth and exserted stamens
